method: Authenticated Firebase Console rules editor and Publish action in the cloud browser.

publication.evidenceSource: Rules version marker and full editor content inspected by the publishing operator before publication and after a complete console reload.

publishedRules.comparison: Exact equality of the full editor content after reload with the approved rules; character count and fingerprint also matched.
publishedRules.hashProvenance: SHA256 computed locally over UTF-8 text with LF line endings from firestore.rules at the source revision. The console does not expose this SHA256; exact content equality links the published text to the local file.

behaviorAlignedWithPublishedApplication: Sala Segura message creation uses the server API; direct client creation is blocked by the published rules.
The published rules are the same reviewed file included in the application revision; publication did not introduce a new rules edit.

priorValidation.environment: Local Firebase emulators with fictional adult accounts.
priorValidation.notes: The rules checks belong to the previous continuity review and are not added to the 563 conversation tests. Online verification checked published content and persistence; it did not perform production data writes or repeat the authorization scenarios.

limitations: Console publication and exact content persistence were verified; no separate production authorization integration test was performed.
Publication time is recorded only to the minute shown in the console; no seconds or server ruleset identifier are inferred.
This action updated only firestore.rules in the existing default database. It did not migrate application data or change account administration, indexes or billing.

historicalEvidence.policy: Earlier records are retained as dated snapshots. Their Firebase-pending state is superseded by this confirmed rules publication.
